articles.title: Artemis Fowl Animated TV Show Greenlit With Eoin Colfer as Executive Producer
articles.summary: Artemis Fowl is coming back to TV screens in the form of an animated show on Disney Channel and Disney+. Author Eoin Colfer announced that Disney had greenlit another series project based on his family fantasy novels at the 25 Years of Artemis Fowl panel at New York Comic Con 2026.
body: Joining Colfer in the executive producing category is Marvel's Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur's Ben Juwono, as well as DuckTales' Colleen Evanson. In a statement, the Artemis Fowl author said he is "proud and delighted to be part of the formidable team that is putting the Artemis Fowl animation on screen."
"Everyone is so talented and so positive that I feel certain the fairy world is in excellent hands," he added.

The Artemis Fowl animated series has no release date, but when it does eventually arrive, it won't be the first swing at the property to land on Disney+. In 2020, Disney launched a live-action movie with the same name, though it largely failed to leave a good impression on fans or critics. As recorded by review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes, the straight-to-streaming film only whipped up a "rotten" 8% from critics and 19% from audiences.
points: Artemis Fowl is coming back to TV screens in the form of an animated show on Disney Channel and Disney+.
Author Eoin Colfer announced that Disney had greenlit another series project based on his family fantasy novels at the 25 Years of Artemis Fowl panel at New York Comic Con 2026.

articles.title: Resident Evil Overtakes Weapons as Zach Cregger's Highest-Grossing Film, The Social Reckoning Bombs
articles.summary: Resident Evil beat Weapons to become director Zach Cregger's highest-grossing film while The Social Reckoning bombed at the box office. The live-action adaptation of Capcom's classic survival horror series turned heads as it reached an estimated worldwide total of $320.2 million over the weekend.
body: Cregger brought his re-imagined Raccoon City to the big screen on September 18, 2026, making this weekend its fourth in theaters. The massive jump – which saw it return to the number one spot, globally – was largely propelled by its premiere in China. Of the whopping $62.65 million it accumulated through weekend four, $40.6 million was earned in China alone. Its victory over Weapons already seemed secure, but as it stands atop Cregger's catalog, it's also continuing to leave its reported $75 million budget in the dust.

Resident Evil's ongoing success in theaters kicked off when it brought in $108.3 million in its opening weekend. It was a strong start that even managed to bleed over into the gaming world with increased sales for some of the games, too, with Cregger's latest also landing as the highest-rated video game adaptation of all time.

articles.title: 10 Best Episodes of 'Buffy the Vampire Slayer' Of All Time, Ranked by Their IMDb Score
articles.summary: Despite premiering almost three decades ago, Buffy the Vampire Slayer still endures. This beloved supernatural show didn’t just lay the foundation for a strong, well-rounded female lead in Buffy Summers (Sarah Michelle Gellar).
body: A successful show that ran for seven seasons is bound to have exceptional episodes. Some are memorable because of the Big Bad featured in them, while others feature crucial character moments or exciting stakes. With these factors in mind, here are 10 best episodes of Buffy the Vampire Slayer of all time, according to their IMDb scores.

This two-part season 3 finale is at its strongest when considered as a unit, but “Graduation Day: Part 2” is a satisfying conclusion to some major storylines. Buffy and the Scooby Gang aren’t alone in their fight against evil, as the entire school bands together to defeat Mayor Wilkins (Harry Groener) and his evil plot to become a giant demon and murder everyone in town. This episode is also a major turning point for Angel (David Boreanaz), who leaves Sunnydale after realizing he cannot provide Buffy with the normalcy that she deserves. “Part 2” takes the show’s “high school is hell” metaphor to its limits, where Buffy’s silent efforts as protector are finally validated.
points: Despite premiering almost three decades ago, Buffy the Vampire Slayer still endures.
This beloved supernatural show didn’t just lay the foundation for a strong, well-rounded female lead in Buffy Summers (Sarah Michelle Gellar).

articles.title: New NetEase FPS Sparks Warzone 'Rip-Off' Claims, But Some Call of Duty Fans Are Happy to See It
articles.summary: Call of Duty fans are torn about NetEase Games' ECC: Redline, a new FPS that many have called a "rip-off" with the power to fill the void for frustrated Warzone players.
body: NetEase called its new shooter a "self-developed extreme-sports tactical shooter" when revealing it just days ago. It's yet another big swing from the China-based tech company that boasts breakneck gameplay on PC via Steam and mobile devices, but in the hours since its big debut, it's also been called a "1:1 rip" of Activision's Call of Duty: Warzone, and it's not too hard to see why.

Viewers say guns look, kick, and move in a way that seems familiar, but the similarities don't stop there. Everything down the UI is being investigated by FPS enjoyers, too, with things like the sound effects also evoking the same kind of gritty action Call of Duty is known for. Even the way the first-person camera blurs when dropping from heights might feel familiar to fans of Warzone and other shooters. Even with characters that present their own unique abilities and gadgets, ECC: Redline has had a hard time escaping the comparisons online.
"Warzone + Delta Force + Blood Strike = ECC: Redline," one YouTube comment left on NetEase's official upload said.
points: Call of Duty fans are torn about NetEase Games' ECC: Redline, a new FPS that many have called a "rip-off" with the power to fill the void for frustrated Warzone players.

articles.summary: Bandai Namco has revealed a first look at Tekken 8 DLC character Yujiro Hanma, and the Baki rep is looking just as uncanny as fans expected. The new trailer for the fighting game's Season 3 characters debuted alongside Evo France 2026.
body: Roger Jr. is definitely the star of the new Tekken 8 DLC trailer, with nearly three minutes of its four-minute runtime dedicated to showing off the marsupial boxer's gameplay. The Yujiro teaser, meanwhile, is tucked at the end, but its reveals are particularly shocking. You can see how the Baki the Grappler villain has been reimagined within the world of Tekken below.

Yujiro is… expressive, to say the least, so nailing his face and bulging muscles was always going to draw attention. Well, the Bandai Namco team did their best, with today's Evo trailer showing just a few shots of his iconic toothy smile and flexibility.

It looks like work on the anime guest character is still underway, but just because there's no release date doesn't mean there isn't a plan to show more. The end of the new teaser promised that a new Yujiro trailer will premiere alongside the Tekken World Tour Finals January 17, 2027. That's three months out from now, so we can probably expect to see gameplay by that point.

articles.title: Robert De Niro's 123-Minute Gothic Thriller Is Officially Streaming on Netflix
articles.summary: Conversely, De Niro’s turn as the detached Louis Gara in Jackie Brown (1997) sparks divisive reactions, while his more recent outings, such as Righteous Kill (2008) and Dirty Grandpa (2016), are considered objective career lows.
body: Robert De Niro is usually associated with complex, dramatic characters who make or break a film. Travis Bickle makes Taxi Driver (1976) feel like a bleak nightmare, Jake LaMotta turns Raging Bull (1980) into a visceral study of redemption, and young Vito Corleone in The Godfather Part II (1974) adds a grounded backstory for the iconic character.

De Niro has also appeared in some surprising roles, such as playing the part of the monster in Kenneth Branagh’s Gothic horror, Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein. Shelley’s groundbreaking book has been adapted innumerable times, including a relatively recent (and wonderful) iteration by Guillermo del Toro. Branagh’s Frankenstein is rather trope-heavy, but it is a strange and harrowing interpretation that's worth watching, in part for De Niro's mournful performance. For those interested, Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein is waiting to be discovered, as it is currently streaming on Netflix.

articles.title: Yahtzee is still out there being mean about videogames, and good for him
articles.summary: When the HMS Escapist sank everyone worth a damn swam away to form a YouTube channel called Second Wind, where Yahtzee Croshaw's video series Zero Punctuation continued under the name Fully Ramblomatic.
body: Back in the Before Times, when someone brought a videogame magazine to school we'd all gather round to flick through it, and the only measure of whether it was a good videogame magazine was if the captions on the screenshots were funny. I didn't notice until years later, but that meant we only read the British ones.

That particularly British tone is something Yahtzee's videos share. It might come across as flippant to some, but to me it's always read as deep care. Putting in the effort to make a description witty instead of plain means you're working harder to keep your audience engaged, and doing that for videogames suggests you care enough about them to want your audience to actually pay attention.

Yahtzee does that. Like Blackadder finding the 100th way to tell Baldrick he's an idiot, he never runs out of ways to complain about videogames. You know how Palworld made a big deal about letting you give your Fauxkémon guns? As Yahtzee points out, to actually do that in the game you have to "jump through so many hoops you feel like a spider in a bowl of Cheerios." That's a throwaway description I bet took the better part of the afternoon, and every episode is full of them.

articles.title: Disney Officially Confirms New 'Die Hard with Fairies' TV Series Adaptation
articles.summary: Disney is officially bringing the action-adventure fantasy franchise Artemis Fowl to Disney Plus with a new animated series, creator and author Eoin Colfer announced Sunday at New York Comic Con.
body: Artemis Fowl follows its eponymous hero, a 13-year-old genius who uncovers an underground world of high-tech, heavily armed fairies. The young Fowl launches a plan to use fairy magic to heal his dying mother and save his family.

Colfer announced the news during Sunday's 25 Years of Artemis Fowl panel at NYCC. He will serve as executive producer on the new Artemis Fowl animated series. Joining him on Artemis Fowl are Emmy and Annie Award winner Ben Juwono ( Marvel’s Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur, Big Hero 6: The Series ) and Colleen Evanson ( DuckTales, Monsters at Work ) who will also serve as executive producers.

"For more than two decades, Eoin Colfer's ‘Artemis Fowl’ books have captivated readers around the world with unforgettable characters, imaginative world-building, and gripping adventures," said Ayo Davis, president of Disney Kids & Family, in a news release. "Bringing this beloved franchise to life as an animated series gives us the opportunity to introduce a new generation to Artemis' world while honoring the longtime fans who have cherished these stories for years."
points: Disney is officially bringing the action-adventure fantasy franchise Artemis Fowl to Disney Plus with a new animated series, creator and author Eoin Colfer announced Sunday at New York Comic Con.

Phoenix Cyclops is first, arriving on 2nd November, with Classic and Legacy costumes for the character launching the same day. Thor (Jane Foster) follows in winter 2027, then Venom and a Klyntar stage in spring 2027. Jubilee is expected to drop in summer 2027.

body: Publisher Secret Mode announced the news on 8th October, after the update was teased at the Triple-I Initiative showcase, the same presentation in which we learned the developer of El Paso, Elsewhere announced Gods With Badges.

The After Party is meant to bring a celebratory vibe to the co-op horror game, with new skins to dress up in alongside the new levels, so we can indulge in a little cake before running screaming from the entities that live in the Backrooms.
Before then, a selection of free and paid cosmetics is arriving in October. It sounds like you'll be able to dress up as an entity yourself, if you fancy scaring your friends.

Escape the Backrooms, from developer Fancy Games, has now been played by more than 12 million people since it launched in Early Access in 2022. It's a one to four-player co-op horror game with more than 30 levels, and is available on Steam, PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2. articles.title: Nier creator Yoko Taro says he's achieved his career dreams, but he continues working because it's 'good for preventing dementia'
articles.summary: They say that art is never finished, only abandoned—but that doesn't seem to be the case for Yoko Taro, creator of Nier and Drakengard, who you might recognize by the round, smiley Emil mask he wears.
body: "With Drakengard, the first game I was given the opportunity to direct, I was actually able to do almost everything the way I wanted," Taro said. "As a game otaku, I think the dream is to release something you've always wanted to create into the world. Having achieved that dream, I view everything after that as the remainder of my life."

As for why he continues to work in gamedev if he's already achieved his dreams, well, he said the money doesn't hurt—and that he has a fear of how his mental health might degrade should he grow idle. "This is good for preventing dementia," he said.

It's worth noting that Taro is, to put it in technical terms, a bit of a silly goose, if the mask didn't tip you off. As the IGN report notes, it's possible he doesn't literally mean that he only works in gamedev to stave off dementia. But that sentiment, as well as his saying that he hopes he can dodge the "flames" of competition from younger, AI-assisted generations before he dies, speak to how Taro views his place in the games industry.

articles.title: Arc Raiders 2.0 is here, and you can finally turn those lights on your backpack off
articles.summary: I remember being a kid and wishing I had shoes that lit up. I know now that I was a fool. If I festooned myself with garish lights, how would I scavenge for supplies in a frozen wasteland without being spotted by strangers who may or may not kill me before I can use my grappling hook to get away?
body: That's one of many little overhauls that arrived in Embark Studios' popular extraction shooter Thursday, and you can read all about the rest in the 2.0 patch notes. If you've not been tuned into the extraction world as of late, you did indeed read that right: Arc Raiders has gotten a big shakeup with the Frozen Trails update, which comes bearing snowy mountains and grappling hooks.

But that's not what's exciting about patch notes—the best part of combing through each little bullet point is seeing all those long-awaited bug fixes and little quality-of-life changes like the aforementioned emissive toggle for backpacks. That and tidbits like "added mouth animation for when players are talking in proximity chat," which I can only hope looks as silly in-game as it does in my imagination.

Some other big, but also small changes include the fact that you can open the map when you're downed now, new contextual animations for a variety of things (your character should look more exhausted when sprinting for a while), and an increased max stash size: 328 without expedition bonuses.

articles.title: "We have to go a different path" - Krafton thinks PUBG Ded.Net's pulpy gameshow hyperviolence and roguelite twist can make it the next big battle royale
articles.summary: Player Unknown's Battlegrounds is arguably one of the most important games to release in the past decade. If H1Z1 built the foundation of the battle royale genre, PUBG certainly shaped it into the form that remains hugely successful today.
body: Fortnite might have stolen the battle royale crown, but PUBG's name still means something even today. So when publisher Krafton announced a brand-new PUBG was in the works last month, it was an immediately exciting prospect for battle royale fans. And doubtless a daunting one for its development team, given the large shoes Ded.Net has to fill.

But what does it mean to make a new PUBG in the shadow of the original? How do you make something familiar, while keeping it fresh enough that it doesn't feel redundant? The answer may lie in Ded.Net; a grungy splatterfest being developed by Krafton's Wisconsin studio, PUBG Madison, that gives those battle royale fundamentals a more rogue-like spin. To find out more, I spoke with creative director Dave Curd about the challenges and opportunities facing the team.

"I was charged with spreading the gospel of PUBG to an audience that might not already appreciate it or like it or understand it," Curd told me at Gamescom. And that required breaking it down to its fundamentals. "What is PUBG? Is it a blue Zone? Is it the level three helmet? I think [it's] desperate survival. I think it's survival of the fittest, it's dog eat dog."
points: Player Unknown's Battlegrounds is arguably one of the most important games to release in the past decade.
If H1Z1 built the foundation of the battle royale genre, PUBG certainly shaped it into the form that remains hugely successful today.

articles.title: Escape from EloHello has me reliving my worst online PvP nightmares in roguelike-form
articles.summary: I was stuck in elo hell for a good four years, then I entered elo purgatory for another five years, and now I'm apparently in elo heaven, but for some reason it still feels like elo hell. I guess that's just part and parcel of playing online competitive multiplayer games.
body: While I'd never want to relive the pain of climbing from Bronze to GM, I am morbidly intrigued in whether I still have that fight in me. So I've found a happy medium, playing a strategy roguelike that provides players with "all the satisfaction of reaching rank 1, none of the toxic teammates or 40-minute hostage games".

In Escape from EloHell, you're set the task of collecting MMR as you climb the ladder from Iron 4 to Challenger, rank 1 in just 60 matches, before the season resets and you have to start again. The only way to gain MMR is to win matches, but unlike an ordinary competitive multiplayer, Escape from EloHell is a roguelike in which you have to gamble on your ability to win matches to gain effects which will help you in the long run.
points: I was stuck in elo hell for a good four years, then I entered elo purgatory for another five years, and now I'm apparently in elo heaven, but for some reason it still feels like elo hell.

videos.title: Tekken 8 - Official Roger Jr. Gameplay Trailer (Ft. Yujiro Hanma Teaser)
videos.summary: Fresh from EVO France, we got the first look at everyone's favorite boxing Kangaroo, Roger Jr! Appearing for the first time since Tekken Tag Tournament 2, this feisty boxing duo excels at getting into their opponent's face and overwhelming them with offence and mixups!
body: We also got our first in-game look at Yujiro Hanma, the final DLC fighter of Season 3, with a gameplay trailer set for the Tekken World Tour Finals on January 17th 2027.
You can get boxing with Roger Jr. when the duo step into the ring for Season Pass holders on November 12th! TEKKEN 8 is out now for PlayStation 5 (PS5), PC (Steam) and Xbox Series X|S.
